message.content: {"caption":"A branching archive tree of numbered coding agents is paired with a line chart showing SWE-bench scores over successive iterations.","description":"The target contains two panels. Left, “DGM Archive Tree”: many small numbered circular nodes form a branching tree, with plain gray connections descending outward from a single root; the connections have no arrowheads or labels. The node numbers are small, and most cannot be read reliably. Node fill color encodes SWE-bench score according to the adjacent vertical color scale, which runs from 0 (dark) to 0.5 (yellow). Border color encodes evaluation group: red means 10 tasks (no basic functionality), orange means 60 tasks, and green means 200 tasks (score ≥ 0.4 and top two of archive). A star marks the final best agent. Right, “DGM Progress”: a line chart with Iterations on the x-axis (0–80, ticks every 10) and SWE-bench Score on the y-axis (approximately 0.15–0.52, labeled from 0.20 to 0.50). The legend identifies cyan “Average of Archive,” blue “Best Agent,” and dark “Lineage to Final Best Agent.” The archive average dips early and then rises gradually; the best-agent score steps up from about 0.20 to 0.25, then about 0.41, 0.43, and 0.50, remaining at 0.50 near the end. The final-agent lineage has two early dips, then rises through about 0.41 and 0.43, dips to about 0.40, and reaches 0.50. Gray callouts with leader lines label “Non-empty patch validation and retry,” “More granular file editing via string replacement,” “Auto-summarize on context limit,” “More granular file viewing via
